title: Depression days and landladies who trusted him with rent
summary: He lived through the Thirties with little money, owing rent to people who believed in him, and he repaid every debt.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Because at that time, them were some tryin' days, what we're talking about now, way back in the Thirties. Them were tryin' days, believe me. Nobody had anything, and there was no work, people weren't working. It was terrible! Nobody had anything. Money just wasn't here. You had apple lines. You didn't know nothin' about that. Apple lines and soup kitchens and all this-that-and-the-other. And believe me, I was walking around enjoying myself like I was a millionaire or something. I don't have a quarter in my pocket.

But I was so happy. I didn't realize, you know, how bad conditions can be. I catch worse times right now. And I've been through it all now, and I'm old and experienced now. I catch it's worse times right now, let me tell you,

than I ever did back in the Depression. Of course, it could have been worse if we was back in them days. But I just happened to be living with some nice people that believed in me, for some reason. You know, I'm sitting at the table with them and eating their food, and one-thing-or-another, and owed them rent... I owed rent and rent and rent. Owe-owe-owe. I mean, they were just nice enough not to say anything to me about it. They believed in me. And eventually, they got their money.

It didn't have to be like that. It wasn't like that with everybody. It wasn't everybody in New York who could say, "I've got a place to sleep and I know I'm going to eat there." And I wasn't worried about it, one-thing-or-another. So I could afford to be... I couldn't afford it, but I mean, I was layin' off and sittin' back and taking what jobs I wanted to take, and which I didn't want, I didn't take. I could afford to do it, because I had a place to eat and sleep, and not worried about being put out. And these people were no relatives of mine either. No relatives, no relations. I was just renting the room, and people thought nothing of letting me live in their home. And they believed in me. If things went bad with me, I'd tell them a bad story, and they believed it. They had faith in me. And it paid off. I mean, they didn't lose nothin'.

I paid up every nickel I ever owed 'em.
I can truthfully say, all my travels I ever did, I never owed rent, the room rent or anything like that. I paid my rent and my food bills, and one of them things, you know. Because I'll tell you, I never know where I got to go back. You never know who you're going to meet in life. So, consequently, I paid my room rent and food bill. Of course, I mean, I don't know... Well, there's a lot of them guys...
